subject: EU1: Staggered service refresh — opt-in & blackout windows
content:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@optihealth.com>, OptiHealth Ops <ops@optihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 08:15:00 +0100
Subject: EU1: Staggered service refresh — opt-in & blackout windows

Hi Liam / OptiHealth team,

Quick heads-up: we’re scheduling a staggered maintenance refresh for the EU1 inference capacity to roll a targeted control-plane/kmod update and driver patch that improves connection recovery and memory compaction. The work will be performed as a series of short rolling restarts over a defined maintenance window to avoid any prolonged disruption.

Planned window: May 4–5, 2028 (UTC)
How we’ll run it: region split into micro-waves; each host pool will be restarted for ~30–90s during its micro-wave. We expect brief TCP reconnects and a small number of in-flight requests to be retried. No model data will be modified.

Impact: transient request retries, rare 1–2 minute cold-starts for long-lived sessions. SLAs remain in effect — we’ll route traffic to compatible pools when available and fall back if any wave shows abnormal error rates.

Action requested: please confirm one preferred 1-hour quiet window (UTC) or opt out of the scheduled automatic assignment. If we don’t hear back we will schedule a default slot for your tenancy during the overall window.

Opt-in form & attachments: redwood-eu1-maintenance-schedule.pdf (attached) and the short opt-in CSV (optihealth-opt-in.csv) to record preferences. You can also reply with your preferred UTC hour or click here: https://redwood.app/maintenance/OPT-12345

If you have strict blackout requirements (e.g., no restarts between 08:00–12:00 CET), flag them in your reply and we’ll coordinate a bespoke slot.

Thanks — we want to minimize disruption and will publish a final runbook 48 hours prior to the first wave.

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Ben — appreciate the advance notice. OptiHealth can accept a single 60-minute quiet window on May 4. Our preferred time is 02:00–03:00 UTC. Please avoid 08:00–11:00 CET on either day; that is our peak data ingestion window.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
- Will long-running streaming sessions be preserved or will clients need to reconnect?
- If our requests are briefly retried, will Redwood surface metrics we can correlate (trace ids / request ids) so our SREs can distinguish retry behavior vs application errors?

I’ve attached our maintenance preference spreadsheet for reference.

Best,
Liam O'Connor

Thanks Liam — we’ve recorded your preference (May 4, 02:00–03:00 UTC) and flagged the 08:00–11:00 CET blackout. Attached is the preliminary runbook (eu1-maintenance-runbook.pdf).

Answers to your questions:
- Long-running streaming sessions: clients will need to reconnect after the host swap. We will attempt transparent handoffs where possible but can’t guarantee TLS session preservation.
- Correlation: we will emit per-request trace ids in the post-window report and provide a CSV export of request ids and retry counts for affected waves. We’ll share a link to the report within 24 hours after your wave completes.

Next steps:
- Marissa / Hannah / Naomi: confirm we have the runbook checks complete (pre-validated rollback steps, load pluggable fallback policy, and Canary watch).
- Liam: I’ll confirm the scheduled slot in HubSpot and share the final 48-hour runbook link.

Links: HubSpot:HS-45678 | Runbooks: https://drive.redwood.app/drive/folders/eu1-runbooks | Maintenance console: https://redwood.app/maintenance/OPT-12345
